historical_record.description: The site, filled from the bay in the early 1850s beside the Greenwich Dock, was still an open wood yard for the Greenwich Dock Bonded Warehouse, with sheds for charcoal and shavings and a rail spur from the Embarcadero.

Built for the City Warehouse Company as a three-storey brick warehouse with a partial attic around heavy timber posts and beams, designed by Percy & Polk — George W. Percy and Willis Polk's brief partnership, of whose seventeen or so works it is the only warehouse, and Polk's first. The Union Can Company, the largest maker of fruit and salmon cans on the Pacific Coast, was its first occupant, until the building came through the earthquake and fire and the company moved away.
All its windows were bricked up, the arched openings left in place, while the Merchants Ice & Cold Storage Company occupied it; the ice company was here for nearly seventy years, until 1975.
Most of the windows were reopened, revealing the original wood sashes still in the attic; offices followed from 1978, among later tenants the San Francisco Bay Club fitness centre.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as an excellent early twentieth-century industrial building and the first warehouse Willis Polk designed.
